correctness.rationale: The source guarantees that a shared bisector-pair polynomial F can be completed to generators of each net and that the locus is represented by J(F,G). Equal loci therefore allow the two Jacobians to be normalized equal. In affine coordinates for a parallel pair, direct differentiation gives J(F,H)=-(2Y-alpha-beta)(2aX+bY+r). Characteristic not equal to 2 makes the first factor nonzero, so the kernel is exactly the three-dimensional span of 1, F, and Y. The quotient by the two trivial generator changes is therefore one-dimensional. Equality of nets forces the coefficient of G_1 to be one after Jacobian normalization, proving that the extra class vanishes exactly for entanglement.

value.rationale: The source singles out nonparallelity as essential to its reconstruction theorem and provides only one counterexample in the parallel case. The new result completely identifies what goes wrong: fixing the same locus and the same parallel pair leaves precisely one extra algebraic direction, and entanglement is exactly the zero value of that defect. This is a natural structural completion of a main theorem/counterexample pair and gives a compact moduli-level description useful when the parallel boundary case occurs.
